Design a computerized adaptive test

Source: R/cat.R
cat_design.Rd

Collects everything that defines an adaptive test: the item bank, how the first item is chosen, the item selection rule, the trait estimator, exposure control, content balancing and stopping rules. The design is then used either live, one item at a time ([cat_start()], [cat_next()], [cat_answer()]), or in a simulation study ([cat_simulate()]).

Usage

cat_design(
  bank,
  select = c("MFI", "MPWI", "KL", "MEPV", "random"),
  estimator = c("EAP", "MAP", "ML", "WLE"),
  prior_mean = NULL,
  prior_sd = NULL,
  start_theta = 0,
  min_items = 1,
  max_items = 20,
  se_target = NULL,
  cut = NULL,
  cut_level = 0.95,
  exposure = c("none", "randomesque", "sympson-hetter"),
  randomesque_k = 5,
  sh_k = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  content_target = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  grid = 121
)

Arguments

bank

An `irt_bank` (from [item_bank()] or [make_bank()]) or a unidimensional `irtfit`.

select

Item selection rule: `"MFI"` (maximum Fisher information at the current estimate), `"MPWI"` (maximum posterior-weighted information), `"KL"` (Kullback-Leibler information over a shrinking interval, Chang & Ying 1996), `"MEPV"` (minimum expected posterior variance) or `"random"`.

estimator

Interim and final trait estimator: `"EAP"`, `"MAP"`, `"ML"` or `"WLE"`. ML and WLE fall back to EAP until the response pattern is mixed.

prior_mean, prior_sd

Normal prior for EAP/MAP (defaults to the bank's latent distribution).

start_theta

Starting trait value for selecting the first item.

min_items, max_items

Minimum and maximum test length.

se_target

Stop when the standard error falls to this value.

cut

Optional cut score(s) on the trait scale for classification testing: the test stops once the confidence interval of the estimate excludes every cut (subject to `min_items`).

cut_level

Confidence level used with `cut`.

exposure

Exposure control: `"none"`, `"randomesque"` (choose at random among the `randomesque_k` best items, Kingsbury & Zara 1989) or `"sympson-hetter"` (probabilistic filter with exposure parameters `sh_k`, Sympson & Hetter 1985; see [cat_sympson_hetter()]).

randomesque_k

Number of candidate items for randomesque selection.

sh_k

Sympson-Hetter exposure control parameters, one per item.

strata

Number of a-stratification strata (Chang & Ying 1999): items are grouped by discrimination and the test moves from low- to high-discrimination strata. `NULL` (default) for none.

content_target

Named vector of target proportions per content area (requires content areas in the bank). Items are drawn from the area furthest below its target (Kingsbury & Zara 1989).

exclude

Items never to administer (names or indices).

grid

Number of quadrature points for interim computations.

Value

An object of class `cat_design`.

References

Chang, H.-H., & Ying, Z. (1996). A global information approach to computerized adaptive testing. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 20*(3), 213-229.

Chang, H.-H., & Ying, Z. (1999). a-stratified multistage computerized adaptive testing. *Applied Psychological Measurement, 23*(3), 211-222.

Kingsbury, G. G., & Zara, A. R. (1989). Procedures for selecting items for computerized adaptive tests. *Applied Measurement in Education, 2*(4), 359-375.

Sympson, J. B., & Hetter, R. D. (1985). Controlling item-exposure rates in computerized adaptive testing. *Proceedings of the 27th Annual Meeting of the Military Testing Association*, 973-977.

Magis, D., & Barrada, J. R. (2017). Computerized adaptive testing with R: Recent updates of the package catR. *Journal of Statistical Software, 76*(Code Snippet 1), 1-19.

Examples

bank <- make_bank(b = rnorm(200), a = rlnorm(200, 0, 0.3), model = "2pl")
design <- cat_design(bank, max_items = 20, se_target = 0.35)
design
#> <cat_design> 200-item bank
#>   selection: MFI | estimator: EAP (prior N(0.00, 1.00^2))
#>   exposure control: none
#>   stopping: 1-20 items; SE <= 0.350
